answer: Coordination Quota Pricing sets each identity’s action budget from a scarce shared resource—computational timber drawn from a per-epoch pool—so duplicate identities must consume separate quota to act. Every new identity must post a fresh quill-signed challenge bound to that pool, and the fee for a second timestamped challenge on the same mesa rises with the count of active identities claiming it. An attacker running N sybils therefore pays N escalating challenge fees plus N quota draws, making mass coordination cost superlinear while a single honest agent pays only the base rate.
